title: The Most Profitable Side Hustle You've Never Heard Of
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The host's opening frames the business as making $30,000 profit in its first two months with zero startup costs. The guest later reports $2,700 January revenue, $21,000 February revenue, an estimated $25,000 March revenue, and a few hundred dollars spent on plants. The guest's detailed figures do not support the opening profit claim.

stated_problem.quote: So bingo is just perfect for anyone but it needs to be you know updated and has more incentives to come out versus just your typical you know win a couple dollars.

idea.name: Plant bingo events
idea.one_liner: Hosts sell tickets and extra bingo boards for social plant-themed bingo events, using venue partnerships and prizes to attract attendees.
idea.customer: Consumers looking for a social night out; the guest says most attendees are women aged 25 to 55.
idea.offer: A hosted bingo event with plants as prizes, entry boards, and optional extra boards.
idea.revenue_model: Ticket sales, extra bingo boards, and private events; private-event pricing is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: So bingo is just perfect for anyone but it needs to be you know updated and has more incentives to come out versus just your typical you know win a couple dollars.
So now we charge $30 per person.
We probably took home about 3,000 and that was after paying two hosts, 200 each.
Yeah, it's very clearly correlated to our views on Tik Tok, to our sales and tickets.

acquisition_channels.details: Organic TikTok and Instagram videos; the guest says views correlate with ticket sales.
Brewery and venue partners share event content with their audiences; neither side pays the other.
Facebook Events and advice to reach local plant Facebook groups.
The guest advises calling restaurant, brewery, and event venue owners.

ideas.delivery: The operators source plants, prepare bingo boards and equipment, set up at partner venues, and host the event; they have also hired hosts to help run events.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Ticket and attendee data would be subject to UK GDPR. Any cold calls to venue owners must be screened against TPS/CTPS. No subscription model or employment-agency model is described.
